|---|---|---|---|---|
| OP — Operating Policy | precedence, product governance, decision protocol, challenge obligation, Git safety, workflow routing | `CLAUDE.md` | always | only agent-behavior policy needed at planning time |
| DEC — Project Decisions | architecture, patterns not adopted, stack, conditional technologies, project defaults | `docs/architecture/decision-register.md` (one register, `D-xx` IDs); optional ADRs in `docs/decisions/` | always (imported by `CLAUDE.md`) | new or changed decision via `architecture-decision` |
| STD — Standards | normative must/default/prefer rules for one scope | `.claude/rules/<scope>/<topic>.md` with `paths:` | path-scoped | the rule file of the matching scope and topic |
| KNW — Knowledge | technique, examples, trade-offs | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (+ private `references/`) | on demand | the skill for that technology |
| WF — Workflows | procedures, steps, stop conditions, outputs | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `.claude/agents/` | workflow invocation | the workflow that owns the procedure |
| ENF — Enforcement | hooks, permissions, scripts, build/format assets | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/scripts/`, root `.editorconfig` and `Directory.*.props` | event or check | the script or setting that checks the owning rule |
| IN — Product inputs | product behavior and approved tunable values | `SPECIFICATION.md`, `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md`, feature/task inputs | read as input | product content only — never engineering policy |

## 3. Respect dependency direction

Conformance dependencies run WF → KNW → STD → DEC → OP; ENF → STD/DEC, declared in its header or a `Conforms to:` comment line. Standards cite decision IDs (`D-xx`) instead of restating decisions; decision summaries exist only in the register. Routing pointers may point anywhere reliably invocable; write them explicitly — after `See also:`, `Workflow:`, `Technique:`, `Procedure:` or `Enforced by:`, or as an invocation (run, use, invoke or switch to a workflow; `→`). The checker treats every other reference as a conformance dependency; references to product inputs and enforcement files name inputs and tools, not owners. A skill's `references/` files are read only by that skill.

## 4. Apply the change

1. Write the artifact with its one-line header: `> Kind: … | Scope: … | Owner: … | Loading: …` (after any frontmatter).
2. Decision added or changed: follow `architecture-decision` § 3–4 (ID, Details in, Affects, propagation).
3. Knowledge skill descriptions stay concise and trigger-first ("Use when …" with concrete cues).
4. Update `.claude/MAP.md`: artifact table, Kind × Scope view, topic index and decision → Affects view.
5. Keep the always-loaded surface (CLAUDE.md, the register, skill descriptions) compact; move detail to the owner it belongs to.

context_quotes:
Goal: restore the affected scope to a green build/test state without hiding failures, weakening behavior or introducing unrelated changes. Use `code-review` to inspect completed changes, `verify` to prove completion, and `build-fix` when a build or test failure already exists and must be repaired.
- Never weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests, compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures merely to make verification pass.
- Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing; stop when progress has clearly stalled instead of making speculative edits.

Use bounded iteration — several focused attempts, not an unlimited edit/build loop. Stop and reassess when the same root failure survives materially different fixes, fixes create growing unrelated failures, the toolchain is incompatible, required external infrastructure is unavailable, package compatibility cannot be resolved safely, or the correct behavior cannot be determined. Do not repeat variants of the same failed guess.

If a fix introduces new failures, decide whether they reveal a legitimate dependency of the change; otherwise revert or correct that fix before continuing. Never leave the repository knowingly worse than where the repair started. Do not clean up unrelated pre-existing failures unless they block verification of the requested repair or the user asks.

Do not claim the problem is fixed while a known relevant failure remains.

1. Identify the concrete failure.
2. Make the smallest appropriate fix.
3. Re-run the affected verification, and build/tests whenever the fix changed code.
4. Repeat until green or until genuine user input is required.

Never hide a known failure or declare completion while one remains. For a stubborn build or test failure switch to `build-fix`.
